code: install.packages("OmopIndices") # install.packages("pak") pak::pkg_install("OHDSI/OmopIndices")

title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
text: OmopIndices adds patient-level measures existing cdm_table. function returns input table one columns added, functions can composed pipe operator. input table must contain person_id (subject_id) , index-based measures, Date column identifies index date. index functions use OMOP concepts supplied conceptSet find records requested window. conceptSet = NULL, package uses corresponding concept sets OmopConcepts available. concept set can also supplied codelist, codelist_with_details, concept_set_expression object.

title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
text: purpose illustrate functionality OmopIndices use GiBleed database contained omock package.
code: library(omock) library(duckdb) #> Warning: package 'duckdb' was built under R version 4.4.3 #> Loading required package: DBI #> Warning: package 'DBI' was built under R version 4.4.3 library(OmopIndices)  cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed", source = "duckdb") #> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data. #> ℹ Adding drug_strength table. #> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object. #> ℹ Inserting <cdm_reference> into duckdb.

title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
text: following example derives several measures cohort. default index date cohort_start_date; use indexDate point another date column. Windows expressed days relative index date, c(-365, 0) means year including index date.
code: library(dplyr)  cohort <- cdm$cohort |>   addCharlsonIndex(ageAdjusted = TRUE) |>   addElectronicFrailtyIndex() |>   addHospitalFrailtyRiskScore() |>   addBMI(window = c(-365, 0), order = "last") |>   addPolypharmacyCount(window = c(-30, 0)) |>   addEthnicity() |>   addLocation()  cohort |>   select(person_id, cohort_start_date, charlson_index, efi, hfrs, bmi,          polypharmacy_count, ethnicity, location) |>   glimpse()

title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
text: reproducible analyses, specify concept set output names explicitly defaults match study protocol. Index functions accept named categories list add labelled categories alongside score, example: addBMI() can select first, last, minimum, maximum measurement window. addEthnicity() addLocation() try values sequentially, makes possible provide fallbacks. Missing values filled corresponding missing*Value argument.
code: cohort <- cdm$cohort |>   addHospitalFrailtyRiskScore(     window = c(-365, 0),     categories = list(       low = c(0, 5),       intermediate = c(5, 15),       high = c(15, Inf)     ),     nameStyle = "hospital_frailty_risk"   )
